_verification_note: Site-ownership verification. Paste ONLY the token, or the entire <meta ...> tag you were given -- both are accepted. The tag is regenerated into the <head> of every indexable page on each deploy, so a rebuild can never silently un-verify the property. Verification must stay in place permanently: removing the token later makes the search engine drop ownership.
_verification_files_note: For the 'HTML file' method instead of the meta tag (Google Search Console, Bing). Map the exact filename to its exact contents; each is written to the site root on every build. Google's file is named googleXXXX.html and contains the single line 'google-site-verification: googleXXXX.html'.
_windows_app_note: The paid Windows desktop build, produced by packaging/windows/build.ps1. 'payment_link' is the Stripe Payment Link shown on windows-app.html. 'delivery_url' is where the installer actually lives: an unguessable URL on a Cloudflare R2 bucket served over its own domain (NOT the pub-*.r2.dev development hostname, which is rate-limited and gives every object a second public URL -- see docs/windows-installer.md). NEVER put the installer in this repository or in ventures/cipher-solver-web/files/ -- the repo and the site are public, so the paid file would be free to anyone who looked; scripts/build_site.py fails the deploy if it finds one. Set the Stripe Payment Link's post-payment redirect to the delivery URL that build_pages.py prints. version/size/sha256 are published so buyers can verify what they downloaded. 'signed' is the publisher name on the installer's code-signing certificate, or false while there is no certificate: the delivery page, the storefront and the FAQ write their SmartScreen passage from it, so a certificate never leaves the site contradicting its own download.
_desktop_release_notes_note: Plain-text improvements keyed by installer version. Only the entry matching windows_app.version is published in desktop-version.json and shown in the desktop update dialog. Pending version entries may be prepared before release without announcing an unavailable installer. Maximum eight bullets, 180 characters each; total manifest must fit 4 KB.

1.2.2: Added user-triggered update checks and version notifications in the desktop window, Help menu and tray, with no ciphertext sent or automatic downloads/installs.
Update dialogs now show the published release's improvements and fixes before you choose whether to open update information.
Added an explicit RSA weakness lab for shared factors, close primes, small private exponents and unpadded low-exponent messages.
Added reused-keystream analysis with pairwise XOR relationships and clearly labelled crib-derived plaintext hypotheses.
Added AES block analysis and supplied-key ECB/CBC/CTR/GCM operations through a maintained provider, with GCM authentication checks.
Added a historical Enigma I simulator with double stepping and bounded initial-position crib search.
Expanded cipher-breaker results with top 5–10 candidates, ranking explanations, close-score comparisons and separate statistical/verification evidence.
Added interactive frequency, IC/entropy and repeat/period analysis, Vigenère key-length hypotheses and ciphertext/plaintext/key alignment beside results.

_stripe_note: Create each product as a Stripe Payment Link, set its post-payment redirect to the delivery_url printed by build_pages.py, then paste the link URL into payment_link below. Change delivery_salt ONCE before your first sale; changing it later breaks existing customers' download links.

stripe._buy_button_note: Optional. Fill BOTH publishable_key (pk_live_... — publishable keys are safe in public HTML by design) and a product's buy_button_id to embed Stripe's checkout on the page instead of linking out. Leave blank to use plain Payment Links. NEVER put a secret key (sk_live_...) here.
